reflections.title: "Why Have You Given Us One Portion?"

reflect.text: The tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh came to Joshua with a complaint about their allotment. They claimed they had too many people for just one share of the land. Because of their large numbers, they expected special treatment from their leader. Instead of trusting God's distribution, they looked for an easy way to expand without having to fight their enemies or clear difficult land.

Their grumbling sprang from pride and discontentment. Rather than claiming what God had already provided through faith and hard work, they chose to compromise and live alongside the Canaanites. In contrast to their grasping attitude, Joshua later waited patiently until every tribe received their land before taking his own small share. God calls us to put away pride and trust His sovereign placement for our lives, which means His wise authority over where we are. We are called to obey Him faithfully and serve Him humbly right where He puts us.

questions: Are you currently complaining about your circumstances instead of trusting where God has placed you?
Where might God be asking you to work faithfully instead of looking for an easier path?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, forgive us when we complain about what You have given us and seek an easier road. Help us to put away pride and trust Your perfect placement for our lives. Teach us to serve You faithfully and humbly right where You have put us. Amen.

reflections.title: "You Can Drive Them Out"

reflect.text: Joshua gave the house of Joseph a strong promise to inspire courage for the road ahead. Even though the Canaanites were powerful and possessed formidable chariots of iron, God assured His people of certain victory. When earthly paths are blocked by difficult obstacles, God invites us to rise up into higher spiritual ground. He does not show us hard tasks to mock or discourage us, but to demonstrate what His indwelling strength can accomplish through praying faith.

For us today, this battle is against the evil around us and the sins within our own hearts. Our old habits and natural weaknesses often feel as unyielding and dangerous as iron chariots. On our own, we are very weak, but as Charles Spurgeon wrote, "the Lord of hosts is with us." True faith relies on God's omnipotent grace, which means His all-powerful kindness. That faith moves heaven through prayer and clears away every stubborn stronghold of sin.

questions: What stubborn habit or difficult challenge in your life feels as strong as an iron chariot?
How can trusting in God's mighty strength change the way you pray about your daily battles?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for promising victory over the sins and fears that threaten to defeat us. When obstacles look too powerful for our strength, remind us that Your grace is far greater. Give us a working, praying faith that trusts You to drive out every evil from our hearts. Amen.

reflections.title: Clearing the Land for God

reflect.text: In this chapter, the people of Manasseh received their territory, yet they failed to drive out the Canaanites who stubbornly stayed in their cities. Like those ancient enemies, evil habits stubbornly try to cling to our lives. We often make weak excuses and say we could not help it, but our hearts have been made over to the Son of God. Sin has no right to remain in a believer. The Holy Spirit is fully prepared to deliver us when we open our hearts to His strength.

Taking full possession of what God gives us also requires clearing away thick growth. When Joshua told the people to clear the forest, he pointed to the hard work of making room. In our daily lives, crowded schedules can easily choke out our spiritual walk. When good activities make us too busy for prayer and reading the Bible, we are carrying burdens God never assigned. We must deliberately clear out that clutter to spend quiet time at Jesus' feet.

questions: What old habits or sins have you allowed to stay in your heart instead of driving them out?
What busy activities are crowding your schedule and keeping you from spending time with Jesus?
reflections.prayer: Dear Lord, our lives belong completely to You and not to our old sins. Help us by Your Holy Spirit to put away every lingering habit that dishonors Your name. Teach us to clear out the clutter of crowded schedules so we can sit peacefully at Your feet each day. Amen.

D4.author: Adrian Rogers
D4.work: When Your Life Is Too Full for God
